This is 41 ✨
Yesterday, my husband @quixotic_king_bar took me to lunch at Le Pavillon—a Michelin-star moment at One Vanderbilt—and I made a very intentional choice.

I don’t drink martinis often.
But when I do, it’s not to escape.
It’s to arrive.

A perfectly chilled martini with Belvedere 10—a single-estate vodka crafted from one harvest, one field, one rye—clean, precise, and deliberate. Served tableside with Kaluga caviar, a fig & blue cheese olive, a Picholine olive, lemon twist, and a side of pristine cold draft ice.

This wasn’t indulgence.
It was mindfulness.
It was alchemy.

There’s a profound difference between drinking unconsciously and choosing an experience with reverence. Yesterday felt like stepping into a future I’ve envisioned for myself—and realizing it’s not fantasy. It’s attainable.

If I’m going to have a martini,
this is how it’s done.

At The View—Manhattan’s only revolving restaurant—the city is constantly in motion. From the 47th floor of the New York Marriott Marquis (1535 Broadway, between 45th & 46th Streets), the skyline drifts by at about 8 miles per hour, while live piano music threads through the room—a fitting soundtrack for the city lights aglow this Monday night before attending a Christmas concert at Carnegie Hall.

After seeing how Danny Meyer’s @USHGnyc perfected fine-dining-with-a-view at @Manhatta, we were confident The View would deliver—and it did. 

We kicked off with a dozen raw oysters, briny and so perfect that we didn’t even touch the mignonette. The baby iceberg salad, with blue cheese, quail egg, and lardons, was a winner. Trofie pasta—with arugula, pistachio pesto, chanterelles, and whipped burrata—hit earthy, nutty, and creamy notes all at once, and the olive oil-poached salmon, with butternut squash farro and pepita gremolata, was quietly luxurious.

The wine list deserves a shoutout for having non-alcoholic wines that felt intentional, not an afterthought—with thumbs up for Woody’s Blanc de Blanc “goes-with-anything” sparkling wine, Dr. Loosen Riesling, a perfect match for our crab cake; and Oddbird Rhone Blend (Grenache, Mourvedre, Syrah), which enhanced our salmon. 

Between the warm service, thoughtfully-prepared dishes, and America’s greatest slowly-revolving skyline, The View is not just a restaurant—it’s a New York experience in motion, one worth returning to enjoy again.

Tonight was a truly special evening hosted by @s.aintjulian from Noilly Prat. What I’ve always loved about this house is the rich heritage rooted in Marseillan Plage in the South of France. The Languedoc-Roussillon region is a second home to me, so experiencing an evening that pays homage to the vermouth of the century felt like a full-circle moment.

With the rise of low-ABV cocktails and conscious partaking, it’s no surprise that vermouth is having its renaissance. This is the new era of sipping with intention. 🍸✨

Julian and the Noilly Prat team welcomed us with a beautifully balanced opening cocktail paired with fresh PEI oysters — a perfect expression of salinity, terroir, and elegance. For the next course, we indulged in a “Reverse Manhattan,” where the vermouth becomes the base spirit. For my main course we had an Upside Martini which was inspired by Julia Childs. It was 5 parts Noilly Prat and 1 part Bombay Sapphire with a twist. 
I paired mine with a rich, creamy vegetarian pasta, and the wine-forward structure of the vermouth intertwined with the dish exactly as intended.

At the end of the day, vermouth is a fortified wine — and that’s the beauty of it. It offers depth, character, and complexity without the high alcohol content. For anyone who wants a cocktail experience without the heavy hit, this is the low-ABV drinker’s dream. A little luxury… without the aftermath.

caption:
Since 1973, upscale restaurant One if by Land, Two if by Sea has operated at 17 Barrow Street in Greenwich Village, founded by Armand Braiger & Mario DeMartini, who opened the restaurant together as both personal & professional partners. The two operated One if by Land, Two if by Sea together for decades, until DeMartini’s death in 1989 & Braiger’s death in 1999, after which it was taken over & changed hands several times. It is currently owned by Gieto Nicaj, who acquired it in 2023.

The 17 Barrow address itself, however, carries significant LGBTQ+ history that predates the restaurant. Built as a carriage house in 1767 & known for its connection to Aaron Burr, historical documentation shows that a restaurant at 17 Barrow Street was popular in particular with lesbians in the 1940s, marking a rare, address-specific record of lesbian social life in mid-20th-century Greenwich Village. Later recollections from patrons claim that “17 Barrow” functioned as a gay hangout or bar in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

When One if by Land, Two if by Sea opened in 1973, it was not explicitly promoted as a gay venue, but the restaurant’s chosen location & founding by a same-sex couple situated it within the broader landscape of LGBTQ+ life & entrepreneurship in post-Stonewall Greenwich Village. Meanwhile, it regularly appeared as a listing in LGBTQ-centric press sources, including The New York Native, After Dark, & John Stapleton’s Weekend Guide to Gay NY.

Today, One if by Land, Two if by Sea is widely recognized as a mixed gay/straight, LGBTQ-friendly restaurant, continuing the address’s long association with inclusive Village social life. It is often a destination for proposals & weddings, including by many same-sex couples. Collectively, these numerous layers establish the 17 Barrow site’s LGBTQ+ significance: its 1940s lesbian patronage, 1960s gay social life, its restaurant’s 1973 founding by a same-sex partnership, & its continued LGBTQ-friendly presence today.

caption:
Есть рестораны, куда приходишь просто поужинать.
А есть такие, где садишься — и будто переносишься в другую эпоху.

One if by Land, Two if by Sea — бывший дом Аарона Берра.
Того самого, чьё имя вписано в историю Америки не только политикой, но и драмой.

Если вы смотрели Hamilton, то знаете:
Берр — человек, который на рассвете вышел на дуэль и смертельно ранил Александра Гамильтона, одного из отцов-основателей США.
Гамильтон умер, а Берр с того дня стал почти призраком при жизни: карьера разрушена, репутация в руинах, общество отвернулось.
Его судьба — тень, раскаяние и вечная попытка быть понятым.

И вот ты сидишь в его доме, где свечи мерцают как будто чуть живее, чем должны, и рояль звучит так, будто играют прямо для тебя.
Слушаешь музыку, чувствуешь историю в каждом шаге официанта по старому полу — и понимаешь: в этом месте эмоции не исчезают, они остаются.

Говорят, здесь иногда слышат лёгкие шаги на лестнице, тихий смех в пустом коридоре, шелест юбки…
А кто-то видел силуэт женщины, похожей на Теодосию, его дочь, исчезнувшую в море.

И девочки… когда мы ужинали и мой партнёр рассказывал мне эту историю, бокал внезапно упал с барной стойки.
Бармен только улыбнулся и сказал:

“Тут никто не ужинает в одиночестве.”

Романтика? Да.
Мистика? Ещё какая.
Тонкое чувство, что ты не просто гость — ты свидетель.

И знаете… это место из тех, что нужно прожить хотя бы раз.
Сесть у окна, услышать пианино, почувствовать, как стены хранят дыхание прошлого — и позволить вечеру случиться.

Я рада, что была там.
Это про эмоцию, про “вау, я действительно здесь”, про ощущение, что ты оказалась в кадре старого фильма.

Но это не место, куда хочется возвращаться снова и снова.
Оно — как редкая книга или музей:
не для привычки, а для переживания.

Один раз — обязательно.
Чтобы почувствовать. Чтобы увидеть. Чтобы понять.

А дальше… Нью-Йорк так огромен, что пусть это место останется красивым, загадочным воспоминанием …

With only ten days left in 2025, I wanted to start this year-end series with one of my absolute favorites—this stunning Napa Valley wedding at The Estate Yountville.

Early October in Napa is pure magic. 
The vineyards are heavy with grapes just days before harvest begins. Within a week, those same vines would be stripped bare. 
But on this day, golden light filtered through full leaves, creating the most romantic natural backdrop.

A wedding this beautiful transcends perfect weather. 
It was the thoughtfulness in every detail, the genuine connection between the couple, and the way their love story unfolded that made it truly unforgettable.

The ceremony felt both intimate and grand. The couple’s dog made an appearance (always a highlight for me), and watching them exchange vows surrounded by loved ones was profoundly moving. 

Then, the reception at The French Laundry elevated the entire experience. The wine cellar moments, the architectural beauty, those blue velvet chairs, and natural light through the greenhouse created frame after frame of timeless elegance.
This is what happens when vision meets flawless execution. These are the weddings I live for.

¿Cómo hacemos nuestros sueños realidad?
Pides, confías, sueltas y no controlas el resultado ….A finales de los 90’s escuche de un restaurante en Napa Valley, California, llamado French Laundry, del chef Thomas Keller, con estrellas Michelin, un concepto gastronómico de granja a la mesa, sobrecreando la gastronomía americana nueva y honrando y recibiendo de la tierra, inmerso entre viñedos en el Valle de Napa. Desde que escuche el nombre me vibró y se me quedo grabado….25 años después, elijo crear un roadtrip para festejar mis 51 años en este planeta, con amigos grandiosos para conocer el Valle e ir a French Laundry…cuando intente reservar, no había lugar y estaba en una lista de espera eterna y casi imposible! Solté la espectativa de ir a este premiado restaurante, y me enfoque en disfrutar de los viñedos, la gastronomía y la compañía….hice mi petición al Universo , confie en él y solté, enfocada en recibir y estar presente con todas las energías y momentos que fueron interesantes…el día que saliamos de regreso, algo me dijo que checara mi correo y ahi estaba…teniamos lugar en este Restaurante imposible de entrar….fue en espacio milagroso…de esas señales que el universo te da para decirte que te escucha, respalda y consciente…La experiencia fue totalmente surrealista y con mucho movimiento y lo mas relevante para mi de esa experiencia al final no fue tanto la comida y este lugar maravilloso e inalcanzable, fué mas relevante en mi el sentir el respaldo asombroso y percibir la complicidad entre el Universo y yo y tener una certeza de que el Universo me escucha y sorprende, de que los milagros y la magia siempre están disponibles si estas presente y dispuesto a recibirlos aunque no se presenten en la forma que tu quieres….
¿Tú que sueño que parece imposible estás dispuesto a pedir, crear y recibir?

Gracias @ingriddalletc @ginoenricco y @chintans1 por acompañarme en este viaje!! Y cuantos mas?

This place has been the hot table in the city, and it makes sense — it’s the sister restaurant of the beloved Fish Cheeks, so scoring a seat is practically part of the experience.

Bangkok Supper Club serves a modern, elevated take on Thai cuisine.
The dishes are beautifully plated and the flavors are clean and refined.
The coconut starter is memorable, the pork belly is perfectly balanced, and the curry is rich without being heavy.
It’s very “Manhattan-style Thai” — polished, aesthetic, and easy to love.

But the real standout is the cocktails.
These aren’t your usual sweet, simple Thai drinks.
They’re layered, aromatic, and genuinely creative.
One cocktail even gets torched right in front of you, filling the bar with warm spice aromas — a little show and a great drink in one.

If you want deeply authentic Thai flavors, I’ll still send you to Elmhurst.
But if you want a stylish night out — elevated Thai food, a cool vibe, and truly good cocktails — this spot delivers.

Reviews (I only included notable ones / my favorites…definetly must tries)
🦀 Uni and Crab Tartlet: Wow. Everything was so fresh. The crab was slightly sweet, the uni was creamy, and the caviar was salty and balanced the flavors out. All the soft textures of the seafood contrasted nicely with the crispy yet delicate tartlet shell. Honestly, a harmonic melody. 
🦆 Foie Gras Duck Breast Wrap: The flavor profile was really different from the uni crab tartlet. This has a more subtle and nutty flavor with a hint of sweetness.
🦐 prawn satay: First of all, the plating was gorgeous. The cashew butter sauce was so creamy, nutty, and rich. The sauce, a piece of prawn, and some pickled onion – the perfect bite. 
 🐚 Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche: DEFINITELY ORDER THIS. I have never had anything like this in my life (probably because I wouldn’t order this on my own..but I guess that’s what tasting menus are for). The watermelon granita was slightly sweet and nicely pickled. Honestly addicting. The scallop was so tender and sweet. A little bit of garlic, granita, and scallop…I am in heaven. Out of all the dishes, this is probably the lightest flavor wise and most refreshing. It is definitely a good palate cleanser dish. 
🐟 Chilean sea bass: the sea bass was cooked perfectly. It was crispy on the top, but still tender. The curry was a little spicy, but so creamy and warming. It had a nice subtle coconut flavor too. The jasmine rice was really good. Since we were seated right by the kitchen, we were able to smell fresh steamy rice every time they opened the rice cooker. It was really aromatic and just made me anticipate trying the rice. 
🐷 Pork Jowl: The pork jowl was crispy on the outside and tender goodness on the inside. The meat wasn’t dry at all. Even though the dish is called “pork jowl,” the main stair for me was the rice. GARLIC RICE. Emphasis on the GARLIC. I LOVE GARLIC. THIS WAS SO GOOD. 

I recommend this restaurant for sure. The service was also very good.

Dining With Bevy: Life With Vision this Fall at @redroosterharlem. There are certain rooms that invite you to slow down, tell the truth, and remember who you are.

This one did exactly that. Sitting in conversation with @bevysmith, a woman who leads with humor, honesty, and heart reminded me that vision is less about certainty and more about courage.

We talked about fear not as something to conquer, but as something to understand… a signal that you’re stepping into territory that requires more faith and more compassion for yourself. We talked about purpose, how it rarely arrives fully formed, and how most of us are simply trying to walk with integrity through the unknown.

I shared pieces of my own journey: two decades of media, entrepreneurship, pivots, micro and macro-aggressions, reinventions, and the quiet truth that I was often “figuring it out as I went.” And yet, even in the unclear seasons, the light never left. It guided. It protected. It redirected.

I left the room reminded that rest isn’t optional, boundaries are spiritual, and impact requires intention. More and more, I’m choosing depth over speed, presence over perfection, and work that aligns with my calling rather than my calendar.

Thank you to my dearest friend @bevysmith for having me and to everyone I met in the room.

건물은 약 120년 된 브라운스톤,
이 자리에서 레스토랑으로 운영된 건 1978년부터,
지금의 Club A Steakhouse로는 2008년부터 약 17년째 운영 중.

오너 Bruno Selimaj는 알바니아 출신 이민자로,
맨해튼 외식업계에서 40년 넘게 일해온 베테랑이다.
그의 철학은 단순하고 명확하다 
“좋은 음식, 좋은 관계, 그리고 진심 있는 환대(Hospitality).”
다먹고 나서 디저트는 on the house 라며 그냥 주시고, 
식사 마치고 나갈때 어떻게 알고 왔는지 식사는 괜찮는지 오너께서 직접 여쭤봐주셔서 더 인상 깊었다. (한국으로 치면 우래옥 느낌이지 않을까) 

‘Club A’의 A는 그의 세 아들(Arben, Agron, Alban)
이름의 첫 글자를 따서 지었다.
그래서 이곳은 레스토랑이자 가족의 상징 같은 공간이다.
지금도 가족이 직접 테이블을 돌며 손님을 맞이한다.

대표 메뉴는 포터하우스, 리브아이, 필레미뇽.
우리는 당연히 포터하우스. 

분위기는 전형적인 클래식 뉴욕.

This now-traditional event brings Serbian Americans in New York together to celebrate community strength and prosperity and friendship across generations. “We are proud to celebrate our 7th anniversary this year, and through our growing initiatives, we are shaping a stronger, more connected Serbian-American community for generations to come. And of course, we are all inspired by Novak Đoković — his perseverance, his spirit, and his unique Serbian never giving up "inat" that continues to inspire us all.” — Marina Schwabic 

We were especially honored to host two distinguished guests:
🌟 Maja Herman Sekulic — the most internationally awarded Serbian writer, poet, Nobel Prize nominee, and global ambassador of literature and poetry.
🌟 John Cappello — former Defense Attaché in Belgrade and Tel Aviv, 25-year U.S. Air Force veteran, President of the Serbian American non-profit Halyard Mission Foundation, and now a congressional candidate in New York’s 17th District.

💫 The evening was filled with friendship, inspiration, and the promise of greater impact. Special thanks to Kire and The Consulate-Midtown for their generous hospitality, which made the night unforgettable!

I’m always grateful to the Chen family and how they accepted my father and I with open arms coming from a different style of Tai Chi. When my Coach Josh Waitzkin came and challenged my Wu style Tai Chi school and proceeded to throw my father and my Tai Chi uncle Bob on the concrete, I was away from class making a movie. When I got the call after the sparring, I vowed to find Josh and beat him at the next @pushhands tournament. 

That didn’t happen. 

But my father and I gave Josh and assistant coach Dan Caulfield new movement patterns in the ring due to the mix of my time competing against pro San Shou fighters mixed with our Wu style pummeling. Josh invited us into his martial home, Grandmaster William C. C. Chen’s Tai Chi Chuan school (then on 23rd street in Manhattan).

My father and I came into the school like respectful challengers, wearing our Wu style shirts with calligraphy from our Sigong (our teacher’s father) ready to fight. I had grown up hearing stories about the Chen school, how they had the best Tai Chi fighters. The stories always felt like the evil Empire in Star Wars. My father and I waited in the lobby where we met Grandmaster Chen’s wife Priscilla for the first time. She called Josh to vouch for us, and we were let into their beautiful space. 

There, we trained harder than ever in the most focused and scientific space we had ever encountered in martial arts, guided by Josh, but led gently by Grandmaster Chen and his joyful method of cultivating innovation. There we met one of my dearest friends, @maximillionchen, and the family’s secret weapon, Uncle Howard. 

My father and I were the first “outsiders” allowed to train in the school, but eventually became formal students of Grandmaster Chen to better understand Josh’s strategies for the team, which leaned heavily on their style’s “inverted breathwork” body mechanics. 

It’s a gift to share space with the Chen family, and seeing them this Thanksgiving with my brother @veganedge1111 was a surprise. I always remember to text on Mother’s and Father’s Day.

Salutations to all those that know how to allow new ideas into their everyday lives expanding hearts. ❤️☯️
